transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I’m here because I don’t feel like I can keep pretending everything is fine. There are these nights where I eat and eat, and afterward I’m just sitting there, looking around at all the crumbs and empty containers, and I feel so ashamed. Disgusted with myself, really. It’s like I don’t even recognize myself in that moment.

And the next morning it follows me. I’ll try to pray, but I can hardly do it because I feel so low and guilty. I go to church and I can’t even look people in the eye the same way, because I feel like somehow they can see it on me, even if they don’t know. It’s just… it’s gotten heavy, and I didn’t know what else to do but come talk to someone.
How often do these episodes of eating a lot happen, and do they happen in secret or when you’re alone?

It’s mostly late at night, when I’m by myself. I don’t like anyone seeing me like that, so yes… it does happen in secret, I suppose. Since my friend passed, it’s been happening at least once or twice most weeks. Sometimes I try to tell myself, “Well, maybe it was just a bad stretch,” but honestly there hasn’t really been a month where it let up completely. It’s like it keeps coming back, especially at night when the house is quiet and I’m alone with my thoughts.
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I don’t have some regular thing I do afterward like a plan to “undo” it, if that’s what you mean. Mostly I just feel awful and embarrassed and kind of sit with it.

I haven’t really noticed myself doing a specific thing afterward in that way. It’s more that I tell myself I’ll be better the next day, or I’ll try to avoid thinking about it, but then the shame just stays there.
Have you noticed feeling down or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like going to church or spending time with friends?

Yes… I have. It’s hard to explain without feeling embarrassed all over again, but after those nights when I eat like that, I’ll be sitting there with crumbs on my nightgown or on the chair, empty containers around me, and I just feel this awful shame come over me. Disgusted with myself, really. Like, “What have I done again?”

And then the next morning it’s not gone. I’ll try to pray, and I can hardly get the words out because I feel so low and guilty. Church has always been important to me, but lately when I go, I don’t feel like myself there. I have trouble looking folks in the eye, even though they don’t know anything. I just feel like somehow they can see how ashamed I am. So yes, I guess I have felt down… especially after those nights.
Outside of these feelings of shame after eating, have you noticed a general loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like going to church or spending time with friends?

I’m not completely sure how to separate it, to be honest. I know after those nights I feel so ashamed that I don’t want to see anybody or do much of anything. But outside of that… I don’t know that I can say clearly.

Church still matters to me. My friends still matter to me. Sometimes I don’t feel as light or as eager as I used to, but I’m not sure if that’s because I’ve lost interest or because I’m carrying all this embarrassment around. It all kind of blends together in my head.

So I guess the honest answer is I’ve noticed I pull back some, but I can’t really tell you that I’ve lost pleasure in everything in a general way. I’m not sure.
Have you noticed feeling down or having little energy most of the day, nearly every day, even outside of the times after eating episodes?

I don’t know that I can honestly say it’s most of the day, nearly every day, no. I mean… I have days where I’m slower or I don’t feel like doing much, but when you say “most of the day” and “nearly every day,” that sounds more steady than what I’m sure I’ve noticed.

It’s hard because the bad feelings after those eating nights can sort of spill over, so I may wake up heavy-hearted and not very energetic, and then I start thinking, “Well, is this just from what happened last night, or is this me in general?” I’m not always good at telling the difference.

But outside of those times, I wouldn’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve been walking around low-energy all day every day as a separate thing. It’s more… it comes in waves, and I notice it more when I’m ashamed or upset about the eating.
How long has this pattern of late-night eating and feeling ashamed afterward been going on? Has it happened at least once a week for several months?

Yes… yes, it has. I don’t like admitting that, but it’s been going on since my friend passed. That’s when I really started noticing these late-night spells, where I’d be up and eating, and then afterward just sitting there feeling so ashamed of myself.

It isn’t every single night, but it’s been at least once or twice in most weeks. And when I think back on it, I can’t really point to a month where it stopped or truly let up. There might be a better week here or there, but then it comes back again. So yes, it’s been several months, and it’s been regular enough that I know it’s not just a one-time thing.
Do these late-night eating episodes cause you a lot of distress, or make it hard for you to function normally during the day, like at work or with family?

Yes… it does. More than I probably let on to people. I’m not working now, so it’s not like I can say I’m missing a job or anything like that, but it’s definitely changed what I’ll agree to do and where I’ll go.

I’ve started turning down bridge nights sometimes, even when I used to really look forward to them, because I get so worried that I’ll be sitting there and someone will look at me and somehow know. Or they’ll ask why I seem quiet, or why I’m acting funny, and I just don’t have an answer that doesn’t make me want to crawl out of my skin.

And at church, I’ve backed away from some of the kitchen duties too. That’s embarrassing to say, because I’ve always liked helping there. But if there are leftovers, or food put away, I start worrying someone is going to notice something missing or wonder why I seem so ashamed around all of it. Even if nobody says anything, I’m just bracing for it.

So yes, it’s distressing. It makes me avoid things I normally would do, especially with church and friends, because I’m so afraid of being seen or questioned.
When you have those late-night eating episodes, do you feel like you can’t control how much you’re eating or stop yourself once you start?

Yes. That’s probably the part that scares me the most, if I’m being honest.

It isn’t like I sit down and calmly decide, “I’m going to have this much and then stop.” Once the house is quiet and I take that first bite, it’s almost like my good sense just… steps aside. I’ll be standing there telling myself, “Belinda, stop now. Put it away. You don’t need any more.” And at the exact same time, my hands are still reaching for something else.

It feels very strange to explain, because I know it’s me doing it. Nobody is forcing me. But in the moment, it doesn’t feel like I’m making one clear choice after another. It feels like once I start, stopping takes more strength than I have right then. I’ll say, “Just this last thing,” and then there’s another last thing after that. And another.

So yes, I do feel like I lose control of it. I may know I should stop, I may even be upset with myself while it’s happening, but I keep going anyway.

Have you ever noticed yourself eating in a discrete period of time, like within a couple of hours, a very large amount of food compared to what most people would eat in that same time, and felt like you couldn't stop or control how much you were eating?

Yes… yes, I have. That’s exactly what happens on the really bad nights.

I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have a little something, but then it turns into much more than that, and it’s all in one stretch, not spread out over the day. Like… I might start with a plate of leftover funeral-luncheon casserole, just standing there in the kitchen, and then before I really come back to myself I’ve eaten that, and then half a pan of brownies, and then some biscuits, and then whatever chicken salad is in the refrigerator.

And when I say “before I know it,” I don’t mean I’m not aware at all. I know I’m eating. I know I should stop. But it feels like I can’t get myself to stop once it gets going. It’s a lot of food for one person, especially in one sitting, and afterward I’m just horrified that I did all that.
